richText: Spring controller documentation
springdoc-openapi
c
reads Spring controller mappings and Java types to generate an OpenAPI document.
The document describes paths, request fields, response fields, and declared response rules.
Swagger UI displays that document and can send requests to the running application.
These features come from an added dependency. Spring Boot's web starter does not include them.
Version compatibility
springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui
c
adds the document endpoint and Swagger UI for a Spring MVC application.
Spring Boot 3 uses the
springdoc-openapi
c
2.x line. The exact supported release depends on the Boot minor version.
Spring Boot 3.5 uses the 2.8.x line in the official compatibility matrix.
Spring Boot 4 uses a different dependency line. Its examples do not apply unchanged to this Boot 3 course.

example.title: Add generated documentation to the greeting application
description: Each example is a separate project. All required application files appear in the tabs.
The commands assume port `8080` and no custom context path or security configuration.
`mvn spring-boot:run` starts the application from the directory containing `pom.xml`. Requests run in a second terminal.
explanation: The first URL returns the generated OpenAPI JSON.
`/swagger-ui.html` is the UI entry path and can redirect to its UI resources.
The UI reads the generated document and lists the detected greeting operations.
The selected controller version determines the operations shown.
No configuration property is required to enable these default endpoints.
`springdoc.api-docs.enabled=false` disables the document endpoint. `springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled=false` disables the UI.

richText: Descriptions and limits
@Operation
c
from
io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations
c
adds an operation summary or description to a handler.
@ApiResponse
c
declares a documented response, including a status that may come from exception advice.
Documentation annotations describe behavior. They do not change the handler's status or enforce validation.
The generated document may need explicit error-response descriptions when errors come from shared advice.
Manual edits to generated JSON disappear when the document is generated again.
An OpenAPI security scheme describes credentials to the client. Spring Security enforces access separately.
A configured servlet context path also prefixes the documentation endpoints.
Security rules can restrict the document and UI paths. Adding documentation does not make protected endpoints public.
Sending one request through Swagger UI exercises that request. It does not verify every documented response.
